headline: Meta launches Waddle World, an AI-powered virtual pet app
summary: The Tamagotchi-like app is available on iOS and Android in the Philippines, allowing users to hatch and grow a virtual pet.
details: Meta has released a new AI application called Waddle World, which functions similarly to the classic Tamagotchi game. The app is currently available for download on both iOS and Android platforms, but only in the Philippines.

Waddle World allows users to hatch and nurture a virtual pet, engaging in activities like feeding and playing with it. Meta emphasizes that the app is designed as a "cozy 16-bit world" for a "warm little escape" and is not intended to be a habit-building tool, chatbot, or productivity aid.

The app also incorporates journaling features, enabling users to record their day via voice or text. The virtual pet then processes these entries, responding in its own voice and adding a doodle. Mini-games are also included for quick play sessions.

Meta has stated that Waddle World is not a chatbot or assistant, and is flagged as suitable for users aged 18 and above. The company is exploring AI companions, following in the footsteps of other AI-centric apps like Pocket and Vibes.

The company has reached out for comment regarding wider availability and will update if more information becomes available. This launch follows Meta's experiments with AI apps and could be a precursor to their AI-powered gadget, Muse.

headline: Amazon unveils Echo Show 16 with Fire TV and Nanomatte display
summary: The new flagship smart display boasts a 16-inch screen, eight woofers, and can run the full Fire TV experience. It costs $499.99 and launches December 16th.
details: Amazon has announced its latest flagship smart display, the Echo Show 16. This new device features a large 16-inch screen and is equipped with eight woofers for enhanced audio.
A key feature of the Echo Show 16 is its ability to run the full Fire TV experience directly on the display, offering a comprehensive entertainment hub.
The Echo Show 16 is available for preorder starting at $499.99, with an optional Nanomatte display for $569.99. A $100 preorder discount is also being offered.
Preorders can be placed now, with the device scheduled to officially launch on December 16th. Amazon is also offering a $100 discount for those who preorder.
The Echo Show 16 aims to be a versatile family hub, featuring improved smart home controls, a better calendar interface, and a real photo frame option.
